paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: Impact of batch size on decoding speed. Evaluated on LLaDA with a single NVIDIA H20; prefill length fixed at 100 tokens.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the impact of batch size on decoding speed, measured in tokens per second (Token/s), for different configurations and methods, evaluated on the LLaDA model using a single NVIDIA H20 with a fixed prefill length of 100 tokens. The x-axis represents batch size, ranging from 0 to 128 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The y-axis represents decoding speed in Token/s, ranging from 25 to 225, also on a linear scale, with labeled tick marks every 25 units. Four color-coded lines correspond to different sequence lengths (L): gray for L=16, blue for L=32, red for L=64, and black for L=128. Each of these lines represents the "dKV-Cache-Decode" method, while dashed lines of matching colors represent the "Origin" baseline. For all L values, the "dKV-Cache-Decode" lines exhibit a steep initial increase in speed as batch size grows from 0 to 20, followed by a gradual tapering off toward saturation. Specifically, for L=16, the "dKV-Cache-Decode" line rises from approximately 30 Token/s at batch size 0 to 202.31 Token/s at batch size 128; for L=32, it increases from ~30 to 183.28; for L=64, from ~30 to 130.58; and for L=128, from ~30 to 81.18. The corresponding "Origin" dashed lines remain relatively flat, showing minimal improvement with increasing batch size—e.g., for L=16, it rises from ~30 to 69.62; for L=32, from ~30 to 59.71; for L=64, from ~30 to 48.93; and for L=128, from ~30 to 35.42. The "dKV-Cache-Decode" method consistently outperforms the "Origin" baseline across all batch sizes and L values.
model_annotations.German: This line plot illustrates the impact of batch size on decoding speed (measured in tokens per second) for the dKV-Cache-Decode method and the original (Origin) method, evaluated on the LLaDA model using a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, with a fixed prefill length of 100 tokens. The x-axis represents the batch size, ranging from 0 to 128 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The y-axis represents decoding speed in tokens per second (Token/s), ranging from 0 to 225 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 25. Four distinct lines are shown, each corresponding to a different sequence length (L): L=16 (black), L=32 (blue), L=64 (red), and L=128 (gray). Each line is represented with a unique marker: solid circles for L=16, solid triangles for L=32, solid diamonds for L=64, and solid squares for L=128. The solid lines represent the dKV-Cache-Decode method, while the dashed lines represent the Origin method. For each sequence length, decoding speed increases with batch size. For example, at a batch size of 0, the dKV-Cache-Decode method achieves speeds of 34.53 (L=16), 36.81 (L=32), 59.71 (L=64), and 118.24 (L=128) tokens/s, while at a batch size of 128, the corresponding speeds are 81.18, 183.28, 130.58, and 202.31 tokens/s. The Origin method shows lower speeds across all batch sizes and sequence lengths; for instance, at batch size 128, the speeds are 35.42, 69.62, 48.93, and 175.95 tokens/s for L=16, L=32, L=64, and L=128, respectively. The gray line (L=128, dKV-Cache-Decode) shows the highest speed across all batch sizes, reaching 202.31 tokens/s at batch size 128, while the black dashed line (L=16, Origin) remains the lowest, reaching 35.42 tokens/s at batch size 128.
